desc: A story pattern: a wrong, judgment on it, a turning (repentance or intercession), mercy, and restoration. Some instances end at judgment.
name: Story pattern: Sin, judgment and mercy

desc: A story pattern: a threat or bondage, a cry, deliverance, the oppressor judged, praise. The text states it in Judges 2:11–19: they did evil, He gave them over, they groaned, He raised up judges who saved them.
name: Story pattern: Cry and rescue

desc: A story pattern: going down — into prison, exile or loss — often a time of humbling, and being raised again, often to a task.
name: Story pattern: Brought low, raised up

desc: A story pattern: god calls, the one called objects, a sign is given, and the mission begins.
name: Story pattern: Called, reluctant, sent

desc: A story pattern: a promise, what stands in its way (barrenness, doubt), and its fulfilment.
name: Story pattern: Promise kept

desc: A story pattern: the word spoken, order made by it, and a presence or memorial at the end.
name: Story pattern: The word brings order

desc: A story pattern: a test failed and its consequence — the counter-shape of deliverance and call.
name: Story pattern: Tested and failed

desc: A story pattern: death, sometimes a prayer, and life given back.
name: Story pattern: Death to life

desc: A story pattern: wickedness, those to be spared set apart (the ark, led out, the mark), a judgment that takes the rest, a remnant left, and sometimes a new beginning. Jesus draws it from Noah and Lot (Luke 17:26–30).
name: Story pattern: Judgment and a remnant spared

desc: A story pattern: a test the text names as a test ("God tested Abraham", Gen 22:1), a faithful answer, and what follows it — the counter-shape of Tested and failed.
name: Story pattern: Tested and found faithful

desc: A story pattern: harm planned, the plan turned back, and good from it. The text says it of itself: "what you intended against me for evil, God intended for good" (Gen 50:20); and Paul says it of all things, "God works all things together for the good of those who love Him" (Rom 8:28) -- read here as the same pattern, stated generally.
name: Story pattern: Meant for evil, turned to good

desc: A story pattern: someone not known for who they are ("they did not recognize him"), then made known ("I am Joseph").
name: Story pattern: Hidden, then revealed

desc: A story pattern: a woman the text calls barren, sometimes a prayer or a promise, and a son born: Sarah, Rebekah, Rachel, Manoah's wife, Hannah, Elizabeth.
name: Story pattern: The barren woman conceives

desc: A story pattern: the elder named, sometimes his protest, and the younger preferred. Stated at the start: "the older will serve the younger" (Gen 25:23).
name: Story pattern: The younger over the elder

desc: A story pattern: a journey to a far country, a well, water drawn, a girl running home to tell it, and a marriage: Rebekah, Rachel, Zipporah.
name: Story pattern: Meeting at a well, then marriage

desc: A story pattern: the people gathered, the covenant read or set out, their answer ("we will serve the LORD"), and the covenant made or sealed.
name: Story pattern: Covenant renewed before the people
